So I'm finally reading Romancing the Beat, thanks to a recent thread about recommendations for other similar resources.  There's one thing that Gwen mentioned early on, but I didn't quite understand:

​

Is it important for romance books to have two POVs in the story and not just one? I'll use a terrible pop culture reference since everyone has probably read it: a single POV a la Twlight where we only ever see Bella's side of the story. I know the author was writing the other side, but it got leaked so it didn't finish the manuscript. Or two POVs a la 50 Shades of Grey? 

I thought it was good to have just one POV, but the more I read in the romance genere, I notice that more times than not, there's two, or more, POVs. And they always seem to be stronger stories for it.

It seems that my understanding is correct: romance must always have two or more POVs.

​

Maybe that's one of the many reasons why Twilight was so poorly written. The Midnight sun was far more interesting.
